title: Isolate KV prefetch service, patch scheduler memory drift, and upgrade async deps
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: The serving runtime shows slow memory growth on long-lived batchers plus variable tail latency under steady traffic. Investigation points to a coupled prefetch path inside the kernel scheduler and an opportunistic prefetch helper that retains per-session buffers longer than intended. This ticket will: (1) extract the KV prefetch logic into a lightweight isolated service (kv-prefetchd) with its own lifecycle, metrics, and eviction contract, (2) patch a scheduler path causing memory drift by tightening reservation lifetimes and switching a hot linked list to a bounded ring buffer, and (3) upgrade async stack dependencies (tokio 1.x -> 1.25, futures 0.3.x) to pick up runtime fixes and better task cancellation semantics.
background: Symptoms observed in prod-ssr region: ~1.8 GB/day heap growth on a single worker after long-running workloads, periodic latency spikes at 99.9th percentile correlated with GC activity and kvcache churn. Heap profiles (pprof snapshots) show retained session buffers referenced from scheduler::prefetch::SharedAllocator. Hunting uncovered an implicit global registry used by the prefetch helper which prevents timely reclamation when sessions are evicted. Upgrading async deps is low-risk but unlocked nicer cancellation behavior and a fix for a tokio timer regression that amplified tail latency under heavy batching.
approach: Design and extract kv-prefetch logic into a separate process (kv-prefetchd) communicating over a simple async RPC (0-RTT over local unix socket) to the batcher; define a compact eviction/lease protocol so ownership is clear
Replace unbounded per-session list in scheduler hotpath with a bounded lock-free ring buffer to avoid pathological growth; add fast path for admission without heap allocations
Upgrade tokio to 1.25 and futures to latest 0.3 patch, run cargo update, and fix minor API breakages; run CI and extended stress tests
Introduce additional telemetry: per-session resident_bytes metric, prefetchd evict_rate, scheduler queue depth histogram, and a tail-latency SLO dashboard
Stage rollouts: canary on a small fleet in staging -> limited production canary (5% traffic) -> gradual ramp with automated regression gating
acceptance_criteria: Heap growth reduced to < 200 MB/day on long-lived workers in the same workload used for investigation
99.9th percentile latency improves by >= 15% under canonical load (batch size distribution mirrored)
No increase in error rates or failed evictions during a 48h limited production canary
All CI and stress test suites (integration, long-run, and race-detector builds) pass
Migration docs and runbook updated, and a rollback plan validated
implementation_steps: Spec: Publish design doc on Confluence with eviction contract (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/kv-prefetchd-design)
Branch: eng/ENG-1012345/kv-prefetchd-extract - implement proto and local socket comms
Unit tests: allocator invariants, lease timeouts, and eviction messaging
Scheduler patch: eng/ENG-1012345/scheduler-ringbuffer - implement bounded ring buffer and microbench
Dependency bump: eng/ENG-1012345/cargo-upgrade - run cargo update, address compile errors, and update CI images
Benchmarks: run perf harness comparing before/after with 24h replay workload and collect heap/latency traces
Canary: deploy to staging, then 5% production; monitor dashboard and hold for 48h
Docs & Runbook: add rollback steps and emergency kill-switch to routing policy
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Inter-process comm increases latency for hot cache hits. Mitigation: use fast unix socket and fall back to inline prefetch for micro-batches; measure extra latency and gate by opt-in flag.
Risk: Dependency upgrade exposes a subtle API change causing deadlocks. Mitigation: run long-run stress tests with race detector enabled; put upgrade behind feature flag until validated.
Risk: Eviction contract mismatch causes double-free or leak. Mitigation: conservative rollout, add invariants and a debug-only guard that emits alerts and refuses risky handoffs.
Risk: Increased operational surface (new process). Mitigation: keep kv-prefetchd minimal, run as sidecar with supervisor, and add health-checks and auto-restart policy
monitoring_and_metrics: Add per-process resident_memory_bytes and rss gauge
SLO dashboard: tokenized request latency p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + heap growth trend line
Alerting: heap_growth_rate > 500MB/day for 3 consecutive days; eviction_fail_rate > 0.1%
rollout_plan: Staging deploy with feature flag enabled for kv-prefetchd. Run 72h soak with the replayed production trace. If green, canary to 5% production for 48h. On success, ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks at each stage. Each ramp step requires green CI and no fired alerts for 1 hour. Rollback: toggle feature flag off, drain sidecars, and revert commit if persistent anomalies observed.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag first: disable kv-prefetchd and allow old inline prefetch path. If that fails, rollback the deployment to previous runtime-1.31 artifact. Pre-approved ops runbook has commands to redirect traffic and force cache warm-up.
notes: Related investigation notes and heap profiles in Drive: https://drive.company/longrun/ENG-1012345/heap-profiles.zip. Early microbench showed 8-12% CPU increase in prefetchd path but a 20% reduction in tail latency when cache hit rates exceed 70%.
